title: Best Mobile App Maintenance Services (2026): How to Hire
description: How to hire someone to maintain your mobile app: updates, bug fixes, store requirements, what to include, price factors and red flags.
intro: A mobile app needs care after launch. Phone operating systems update every year, app stores change their rules, libraries need security fixes and users find bugs. Without maintenance, apps slowly break, lose ratings and can be removed from stores. Maintenance goes wrong when nobody has the code or accounts, or the scope of support is unclear. This guide helps you set up reliable care for your app.

faq.a: Typically operating system compatibility updates, library and security updates, bug fixes, crash monitoring, store requirement changes and small improvements.

faq.q: Can a new developer maintain an app someone else built?
faq.a: Usually yes, if you have the full source code, build instructions and access to accounts. Expect them to spend some time getting familiar with the code first.

faq.q: How often does an app need updates?
faq.a: At least when major iOS and Android versions are released, and whenever the stores change their requirements. Many apps also ship small updates every few weeks.
A tool that reports when and why the app crashes on users' devices. It helps fix problems users never report.

faq.q: Monthly plan or pay per task?
faq.a: Monthly plans suit apps that change regularly. Per-task work suits stable apps that only need occasional updates.
